FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.subtitle: Learn more about LM Speed X

performance.question: How does LM Speed X conduct performance testing?
performance.answer: LM Speed X employs a five-round continuous stress testing mechanism. Token calculations are performed accurately using tiktoken.

comparison.question: How to compare performance between different API providers?
comparison.answer: Through standardized performance testing and ranking features, you can visually compare the performance of different providers' APIs. The system automatically analyzes and displays comparative data for various performance metrics, helping you choose the most suitable model and provider.

monitoring.question: Is my API key secure?
monitoring.answer: LM Speed X never uploads your API key to any server. All tests are initiated directly from your browser. Your key is only stored in browser localStorage and can be cleared at any time.

dataStorage.question: Where are my test data stored?
dataStorage.answer: All test results and ranking data are stored in your browser's localStorage. You can manage them via Developer Tools → Application → Storage → Local Storage. Data is stored locally only — clearing browser data will lose your test records.

urlParams.question: Can I start a test automatically via a link?
urlParams.answer: Yes. Fill in your API details and click the "Generate Link" button to get a link with all your configuration. The link starts the test automatically on page load by default. Click "Generate Link" again for a plain link without auto-start.

providerSupport.question: Which API providers and models are supported?
providerSupport.answer: Any provider compatible with the OpenAI API format is supported, including OpenAI, DeepSeek, Silicon Flow, Tencent Cloud, Alibaba Cloud Bailian. Provide the correct Base URL, API Key, and Model ID to test any OpenAI-compatible model.

Changelog.title: Changelog
Changelog.subtitle: LM Speed X version update history

v0_11_0.sharedConnection: Stability and concurrency tests now share the connection settings with the speed test
v0_11_0.sharedConnectionDetail: The direct-connect switch and custom headers take effect there: headers entered here used to be ignored, and requests still went through the server proxy even with direct connect on
v0_11_0.sharedConnectionTimeout: Request timeouts now match the speed test, so a stalled upstream reports a clear timeout instead of spinning forever
v0_11_0.stabilityPartialFailure: A failed run no longer aborts the whole stability test
v0_11_0.stabilityPartialFailureDetail: Failed runs are marked in red with the reason, the summary counts only successful runs, and the number of failures is reported at the end
v0_11_0.concurrencyFirstToken: The first-token wait limit now applies to browser-direct concurrency tests too
v0_11_0.concurrencyFirstTokenDetail: The setting used to work only through the server proxy and was ignored in direct mode
v0_11_0.concurrencyProgress: Progress advances per completed request in each level and shows the elapsed wait time

v0_10_7.autoCompleteSwitch: New "Auto-complete API URL" switch in Extra Settings
v0_10_7.autoCompleteSwitchDetail: When off, the address is used exactly as typed: no http(s):// prefix, no endpoint stripping and no automatic /v1 suffix
v0_10_7.browserDirectHint: Browser direct mode covers tunnel addresses and tells you when it kicks in
v0_10_7.browserDirectHintDetail: Intranet and tunnel addresses (including the 100.64.0.0/10 range) enable browser direct mode automatically; after you pick an address, a notice in the bottom-right corner reports the current mode and offers one-click enabling when the address uses a custom port

v0_10_6.removeInstallButton: Removed the "Install app" button from the header
v0_10_6.removeInstallButtonDetail: The install entry now lives entirely in the browser (address-bar install icon / the install item in the browser menu); the page no longer duplicates it

v0_10_5.installGuideByBrowserDetail: Chrome / Edge, Android Chrome, iOS Safari, macOS Safari, Firefox and in-app browsers now each get accurate instructions instead of the generic "look for the address-bar icon" hint
v0_10_5.installEntryRestore: Handed the install entry back to the browser: the address-bar install icon and the browser menu install item show up again
v0_10_5.installEntryRestoreDetail: The beforeinstallprompt event is no longer intercepted; the "Install app" button now explains where the entry is and notes when the browser has offered it

v0_10_4.installPrompt: In-app install entry: new "Install app" button in the header that opens the browser's native install dialog
v0_10_4.installButton: Opens the browser's native install dialog when available; when no install event is offered (HTTP non-secure context, iOS / Firefox), it shows step-by-step manual install guidance instead; hidden once installed
v0_10_4.offlineStartFix: Fixed blank screen when launching offline
v0_10_4.offlineStartFixDetail: The installed app's start_url is /; offline, the service worker's fallback returned a redirect response, which browsers reject (net::ERR_FAILED). The response is now rebuilt and the cache version bumped
v0_10_4.emptyBaseUrlFix: Fixed the API URL being auto-filled with /v1 when opening the model list with an empty address
v0_10_4.emptyBaseUrlFixDetail: An empty address is no longer normalized to /v1 and written back into the input; the form now asks for the Base URL and skips probing the current site

v0_10_3.autoFixUrlInput: Automatic normalization of API URL input
v0_10_3.schemeEndpoint: Scheme-less addresses get http(s) auto-completed (http for private/CGNAT hosts); pasted full endpoints (/chat/completions, /models) are stripped back to the base address
v0_10_3.autoFixApiUrl: Automatic API URL fixing with /v1 fallback
v0_10_3.fallbackToV1: When the filled-in URL lacks /v1, the address is requested as-is first and /v1 is appended automatically when it fails; browser-direct and server-proxy share one logic and the corrected URL is written back to the input

v0_10_2.clipboardFallback: Clipboard permission detection for config import/export
v0_10_2.manualCopyPaste: When the clipboard is unavailable, a dialog opens for manual copy of exported content and manual paste of imported content

v0_10_1.resultFilter: Connectivity check results now support status filtering
v0_10_1.filterByStatus: Filter by success / warning / failed status, or view all results — all shown by default
v0_10_1.copyFilteredResults: The copy-model-IDs button now copies whatever the current filter shows

v0_7_4.storageLimit: Added a storage cap for test results (max 500 entries); oldest results are automatically trimmed when exceeded
v0_7_4.stabilityFixes: Stability fixes: browser-direct mode for local/private APIs, streamed result loss, ranking page crash, import data bloat, and more

v0_8_0.cfDetect: Auto-detects Cloudflare challenge interception and prompts manual verification
v0_8_0.cfManualVerify: Supports embedded panel / popup window for completing Cloudflare challenge; auto-switches to browser-direct model fetch after verification

v0_8_1.cfConnectivityFix: Fixed the connectivity check failing to recognize Cloudflare interception when fetching the model list
v0_8_1.sharedDetection: Extracted shared modules for Cloudflare challenge detection and model authenticity validation

v0_8_2.cfDialogFix: Fixed the verification dialog not popping up when a Cloudflare challenge is detected
v0_8_2.cfStructuredSignal: The server now returns a structured cfUrl field; the client opens the manual verification dialog automatically upon detection
v0_8_2.cfFallbackMatch: Fallback error-message matching: the verification dialog still opens even when the structured field is missing

v0_8_3.autoDelayThresholdLowered: Lowered the auto-delay threshold from 100 to 20 models to avoid hitting API rate limits
v0_8_3.defaultTimeout60s: Added a 60-second default timeout so a single slow model no longer blocks all subsequent checks

v0_9_0.themeToggle: Theme switcher in the header — Light / Dark / Follow system
v0_9_0.followSystem: Follows your system appearance by default
v0_9_0.configValidation: Config validation improvements for test buttons
v0_9_0.jumpToConfig: All three test buttons: clicking without config jumps to the form and highlights the missing fields
v0_9_0.localizedErrors: Validation error messages are now fully localized (Chinese/English)

v0_10_0.pwa: PWA offline support — installable and usable without a network
v0_10_0.installable: Install to your desktop / home screen and run in a standalone window
v0_10_0.offlineCache: Static assets are cached locally, so the app opens and shows past test results even when offline
v0_10_0.apiOnlineOnly: Speed-test and other requests always run in real time over the network, never from a stale cache

v0_7_3.visionVerify: Added image recognition verification to the connectivity check
v0_7_3.verifyVision: Sends a red circle image to the model to verify image understanding capability

v0_1_0.realtime: Real-time performance monitoring with multi-dimensional data display
v0_1_0.streaming: Streaming results for real-time test progress monitoring
v0_1_0.ranking: Speed rankings to compare performance across models and providers
v0_1_0.export: One-click export for test reports and sharing

v0_2_0.localStorage: Migrated data storage from remote database to browser localStorage, eliminating the need for a backend database

v0_3_0.rename: Officially renamed to LM Speed X

v0_5_0.concurrencyOpt: Concurrency optimization: prevent fake concurrency, add max first token latency and timeout mechanism

v0_5_1.localNetwork: Fixed browser-based public link to test intranet environments

v0_6_1.connStatus: Optimized connectivity test status display: test success, failure, and plan-limited tiered statuses

v0_7_0.verifyRepeat: PONG test: requests a specific word from the model to verify basic response capability
v0_7_0.verifySelf: Self-identification test: asks model to state its own name to detect proxy models posing as general AI
v0_7_0.verifyMath: Math verification: asks model to solve an arithmetic problem to verify actual reasoning ability

v0_7_1.projectCleanup: Cleaned up project structure: removed database-related leftovers and redundant files
v0_7_1.projectInfo: Refactored project information: updated README structure and deployment docs
v0_7_1.connectivitySort: Fixed connectivity check sorting: results with the same status are now ordered by latency ascending

v0_7_2.baseUrlAddFix: Fixed built-in base URLs failing to be selected via custom input
v0_7_2.connectivityAutoDelay: Connectivity check now supports 100+ models: auto-adds a request interval to prevent excessive concurrency; can be set to 0 for parallel testing
v0_7_2.exportModelIds: Connectivity check: one-click batch export of available model IDs (comma-separated) to clipboard

CloudflareBypass.note: After verification, the browser stores a cf_clearance cookie for this domain. Model listing will then use direct browser fetch. If it still fails, try a different API or ask the provider to disable Cloudflare protection.
